mainTopic: When witnesses make a defendant a הוחזק כפרן, and the scholars' laughter at רבי שמעון's comparison of שבועת העדות to שבועת הפקדון
overview: The amud opens by finishing a question: if witnesses watched from outside as money was counted, what is the law? רב המנונא answers that it depends on the defendant's claim. If he says 'it never happened,' the witnesses prove him a הוחזק כפרן. If he says 'I took my own money,' the witnesses add nothing, and רב יהודה praises him. Next comes the story of the man who denied passing a column, where witnesses saw him urinate. In one version ריש לקיש calls him a כפרן, and רב נחמן objects that he only meant 'not for this loan.' In another version the man said 'ever,' so רב נחמן calls him a כפרן, and רבא answers that people forget unimportant things. The גמרא then returns to רבי שמעון, who learns from פקדון that שבועת העדות applies only to money. The scholars of ארץ ישראל laughed at his ברייתא, and the גמרא tries several explanations of the joke. Along the way it decides that פקדון is learned from מעילה, not עדות, because more features are shared. The amud ends with a challenge: through the גזירה שוה, עדות should then take the rule that a deliberate false oath brings no קרבן.

steps.title: What if witnesses watched from outside?
steps.stepSummary: The question asked just before this line ends here: if money was counted in private but witnesses saw it from outside, what is the law?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if witnesses see him counting the money from outside, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes a question that began just before this passage. Someone counted money for another person in private, and witnesses saw it from outside; what is the law? The next step gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is tricky because the witnesses saw money being handed over, but they did not hear what it was for. The question is whether their testimony counts for anything. That depends on what the other side claims.

keyTerms.meaning: Witnesses
From outside
What (is the law)?

phrases.english: And witnesses see him from outside — what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a question that began before this passage.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether witnesses who saw money counted from outside, without hearing what it was for, can make a difference in the case.

steps.title: It depends on what the defendant claims
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא answers by asking what the defendant says. If he denies the whole thing, the witnesses prove him a liar. If he admits taking money but says it was his own, the witnesses prove nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא said to him: What does the other person claim? If he says, 'These things never happened,' he is established as a denier. If he says, 'Yes, I took money, but it was my own money that I took,' then when the witnesses come, what difference does it make?
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא answers the question by splitting it into two possible claims the defendant might make.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Witnesses only matter if they contradict what the defendant actually says. A total denial ('it never happened') is contradicted, since they saw money handed over, so he becomes a הוחזק כפרן. But if he says 'I took my own money,' the witnesses agree money moved and cannot say why, so his claim stands.

keyTerms.meaning: And what does the other person claim?
These things never happened (a total denial)
He is established as a denier, proven to have lied
It was my own (money) that I took

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the key idea for the rest of the passage: witnesses make someone a כפרן only if they truly contradict his specific claim.

phrases.english: Rav Hamnuna said to him:
And what does the other one claim?
If he says: 'These things never happened' —
he is established as a denier!
If he says: 'Yes, I took it —
but it was mine that I took' —
when witnesses come, what difference does it make?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הַמְנוּנָא וְהַלָּה מָה טוֹעֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The witnesses matter only if the defendant totally denies the event. If he admits taking the money but says it was his own, their testimony adds nothing.

steps.title: רב יהודה praises רב המנונא
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה is impressed by the answer and warmly invites רב המנונא in.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Are you המנונא? Come in!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה reacts to the answer with admiration, which shows he accepts it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'Are you המנונא? Come in' are a warm compliment. They show that רב יהודה agrees with the answer, so the first discussion ends here.

keyTerms.meaning: Enter, come (in)

steps.whatToRemember: Witnesses who saw money handed over only hurt a defendant who denies the whole event. A defendant who says 'it was my own money' is not contradicted by them.

phrases.english: He said to him: Are you Hamnuna?
Come in!
phrases.notes: This is praise: he is so sharp he deserves to come right in and join the learning.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הַמְנוּנָא אַתְּ עוּל תָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts and praises the answer from step 2.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב המנונא's two-sided analysis is accepted.

steps.title: The man by the column: ריש לקיש's ruling
steps.stepSummary: A man claimed he lent money next to a column. The defendant said he did not pass that column. Witnesses saw him urinate there, and ריש לקיש rules he is a הוחזק כפרן.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a man who said to his friend, 'I counted out a מנה for you next to this column.' The friend said, 'I did not pass by this column.' Two witnesses came and testified that he urinated next to this column. ריש לקיש said: He is established as a denier.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a new story about a similar issue and gives ריש לקיש's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The witnesses did not see any loan. They only proved that the defendant was at the column at some point. ריש לקיש reads 'I did not pass this column' as a flat statement about ever being there, so the witnesses catch him in a lie and he becomes a כפרן.

keyTerms.meaning: A מנה, a sum of one hundred dinars
Next to this column
Two witnesses

phrases.english: There was a certain man who said to his friend:
'I counted out a maneh for you next to this column,'

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: ״לֹא עָבַרְתִּי בְּצַד עַמּוּד זֶה״.
phrases.english: He said to him: 'I did not pass by this column.'
Two witnesses came,

phrases.aramaic: אַסְהִידוּ בֵּיהּ דְּהִשְׁתִּין מַיִם בְּצַד עַמּוּד זֶה.
phrases.english: and testified about him that he urinated next to this column.
Reish Lakish said:
He is established as a denier.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story about the same theme of when someone becomes a הוחזק כפרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A defendant who claims he never passed the column, and is shown by witnesses to have been there, is a הוחזק כפרן.

steps.title: רב נחמן: He only meant 'not for this loan'
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן strongly rejects ריש לקיש's ruling. The defendant never said he was never at the column at all; he meant he was not there for this loan.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן objected: That is a Persian-style ruling! Did he say 'ever'? He was talking about this matter!
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן attacks ריש לקיש's ruling, calling it unfair, and explains what the defendant really meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People speak in context. 'I did not pass this column' in a fight about a loan means 'I did not pass it to get a loan from you.' The witnesses only showed he was there for another reason, so they do not contradict him. This matches רב המנונא's idea: witnesses make someone a כפרן only if they truly contradict what he claimed.

keyTerms.meaning: He objects to it (a strong challenge)
A Persian ruling, meaning an unfair, unreasonable judgment
Ever, at all
Regarding this matter (this loan)

steps.confusionAlert: רב נחמן is not saying the witnesses are lying. He agrees the man urinated by the column. He is saying that fact does not contradict what the defendant meant.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב נחמן, we read a defendant's denial in context. Witnesses who catch him on an unrelated detail do not make him a כפרן.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman objects to it:
This is a Persian ruling!
phrases.notes: He means it is harsh and unreasonable, the kind of judgment a non-Jewish court might give.

phrases.english: Did he say 'ever'?!
He was telling him about this matter!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly attacks ריש לקיש's ruling from step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's ruling that the defendant is a הוחזק כפרן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The defendant's denial was about this loan only, not about ever being at the column. So the witnesses who saw him urinate there do not contradict him.

steps.title: Another version: רב נחמן rules the column denier is a liar
steps.stepSummary: In an alternate telling of the column story, רב נחמן rules that the man who denied ever passing the column is a הוחזק כפרן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say the story went like this: A man told another, "I counted out a מנה for you next to this column." The other answered, "I never passed next to this column." Witnesses testified that he had urinated next to that column. רב נחמן said: He is established as a denier.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא retells the same column story in a different version. This time it is רב נחמן, not ריש לקיש, who rules that the man is a proven liar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key change is the word 'מעולם' (ever). In the first version, רב נחמן's objection was exactly that the defendant never said 'ever'. Here the defendant does say 'ever', so the witnesses contradict his actual words, and רב נחמן rules he is a הוחזק כפרן.

keyTerms.meaning: Column, pillar
Witnesses (Aramaic)
Ever, never in my life

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two versions. In the first version the defendant did not say 'ever', and רב נחמן rejects the 'liar' ruling. In this version the defendant says 'ever', and רב נחמן himself makes that ruling.

phrases.english: There are those who say:
A certain man who said to his fellow:
"I counted out a maneh for you
phrases.notes: A מנה is one hundred dinars.

phrases.english: next to this column."
He said to him: "I did not pass
next to this column, ever."
Witnesses came out about him
that he urinated next to this column.
Rav Nachman said: He is established as a denier.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Retells the case from steps 4 and 5. Here the defendant says 'ever', and רב נחמן rules he is a הוחזק כפרן, which fits his objection in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who denies ever passing a place, and witnesses saw him there, is a הוחזק כפרן.

steps.title: רבא: People do not remember unimportant things
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges רב נחמן. A person does small things without paying attention, so forgetting that he passed the column does not make him a liar.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רב נחמן: Anything that a person has no reason to keep in mind, he does without it being on his mind.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא argues against רב נחמן's ruling in this version. He says the man may simply not have remembered passing the column.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן treated the denial as a lie. רבא says urinating by a column is not something anyone bothers to remember. So the man's words 'I never passed there' can be an honest mistake, not a proven lie.

keyTerms.meaning: A matter, a thing
Is placed on him: something he needs to pay attention to
On his mind, in his awareness

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, denying something unimportant that a person might simply have forgotten does not make him a כפרן, even if he said 'ever'.

phrases.english: Rava said to Rav Nachman:
Any matter that is not placed
phrases.notes: Literally 'not thrown on him.' He means something the person has no need to keep track of.

phrases.english: upon a person,
he does it and it is not on his mind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling of step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling that the man is a הוחזק כפרן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: People do not remember unimportant actions, so a denial of such an action is forgetfulness, not proof of lying.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: Compare the witness oath to the deposit oath
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא and quotes רבי שמעון. He learns that שבועת העדות applies only to money by comparing it to the oath about a פקדון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: The Torah made one liable here, and it made one liable with a deposit. (Just as there it is about money, so too here.)
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the ברייתא about where we learn that שבועת העדות is only about money claims, and quotes רבי שמעון's source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון links the two oaths. The oath about a פקדון is clearly about money, so the oath of witnesses must also be only about money. This is a new topic after the column stories.

keyTerms.meaning: Made liable (the Torah obligated a קרבן)
Here: in שבועת העדות
An item deposited with someone for safekeeping
Etc.: the rest of the quote is assumed

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
He made liable here
and He made liable with a deposit, etc.
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' stands for the rest: just as the deposit oath is about money, so is this one.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: חִיֵּיב כָּאן וְחִיֵּיב בְּפִקָּדוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the column stories and returns to the ברייתא's list of sources.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שבועת העדות applies only to money claims, learned by comparing it to the oath about a פקדון.

steps.title: The West laughed at it: what was funny?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reports that the scholars of ארץ ישראל laughed at רבי שמעון's proof and asks what the laughter was about.
steps.simpleTranslation: They laughed at it in the West. What was the laughter about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says רבי שמעון's proof was laughed at in ארץ ישראל and asks why. This line sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Laughing at a proof means they thought it had a basic flaw. The גמרא does not say the flaw yet. It asks 'מאי חוכא' so the next lines can explain what was wrong with the comparison.

keyTerms.meaning: They laughed, mocked
The West: ארץ ישראל
Laughter, mockery

phrases.english: They laughed at it in the West.
phrases.notes: 'The West' is ארץ ישראל, which is west of בבל.

phrases.english: What is the laughter?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reports an objection to רבי שמעון's proof from step 8 and asks for its reason.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What flaw the scholars of ארץ ישראל saw in רבי שמעון's comparison to the oath about a פקדון.

steps.title: The laughter was aimed at the ברייתא's distinction
steps.stepSummary: The scholars laughed at the ברייתא's line that פקדון is different from עדות in two ways: an oath put on him by others, and an intentional oath compared to an unintentional one.
steps.simpleTranslation: They laughed at what the ברייתא teaches: 'What about a פקדון? It is different, because there the Torah did not treat one who had an oath put on him like one who swore himself, and it did not treat an intentional oath like an unintentional one.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 9 by pointing to the exact line in the ברייתא that the scholars laughed at.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא had tried to block a comparison between עדות and פקדון by listing two ways they are different. The scholars of ארץ ישראל found this rejection laughable. The גמרא now has to explain why.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who had an oath put on him by others, who answers 'אמן'
Someone who swears by himself, in his own words
On purpose, knowingly
By mistake, without knowing

phrases.english: At what it teaches:
What about a deposit?
It is different, since [the Torah] did not make there
one who had an oath put on him like one who swore himself,
[or] an intentional one like an unintentional one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 9's question about what the laughter was about.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The laughter was aimed at the ברייתא's line separating פקדון from עדות.

steps.title: If עדות learns from פקדון, פקדון should learn from עדות
steps.stepSummary: The scholars' complaint: רבי שמעון learns from פקדון that a self-sworn oath counts for עדות, so פקדון should likewise learn from עדות that an oath put on him by others counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: After all, for עדות, where does רבי שמעון get that one who swore by himself is liable? He learns it from פקדון. Then פקדון too should learn from עדות that one who had the oath put on him by others is liable!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the first explanation of why the scholars laughed. The ברייתא's first difference makes no sense to them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The assumption is that עדות and פקדון are linked to each other, so they share their rules. If עדות borrows the 'swore by himself' rule from פקדון, then פקדון should borrow the 'oath from others' rule from עדות. In that case 'מושבע כנשבע' is not a real difference between them.

keyTerms.meaning: After all, since (opens an argument based on what we already know)
From his own mouth, sworn by himself
From the mouth of others, an oath put on him by someone else
He learns it, by comparing one case to another

phrases.english: After all, one who swore by himself regarding testimony,
according to רבי שמעון, from where does he know it?
He learns it from the deposit.
Then for a deposit too, one who had the oath put on him by others,
let us learn it from testimony!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the line quoted in Step 10 was laughable.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's first difference: that in a פקדון, an oath put on him by others does not count like one he swears himself.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A two-way link means each case borrows from the other. If עדות borrows from פקדון, then פקדון should borrow back from עדות.

steps.title: רבי שמעון may have used a קל וחומר instead
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the explanation: maybe רבי שמעון never borrowed from פקדון, and learned his rule for עדות through a קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what is there to laugh at? Maybe רבי שמעון learns it through a קל וחומר: if one is liable when others put the oath on him, then surely he is liable when he swears by himself!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back and says the first explanation of the laughter does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The complaint in Step 11 only works if עדות got its 'swore by himself' rule from פקדון. If רבי שמעון got that rule from a קל וחומר inside עדות itself, then nothing was borrowed from פקדון. So פקדון has no reason to borrow back from עדות, and the ברייתא's difference stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Laughter, mockery
Perhaps, maybe
An argument that if a rule applies in the weaker case, it surely applies in the stronger case
All the more so

phrases.english: And what is there to laugh at?
Perhaps רבי שמעון
brings it through a קל וחומר:
[if when the oath comes] from others he is liable,
[when it comes] from himself, all the more so!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי חוּכָא? דִּלְמָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּקַל וָחוֹמֶר מַיְיתֵי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects Step 11's explanation of the laughter.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the idea that the laughter was about 'מושבע כנשבע'.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumes רבי שמעון learned the 'swore by himself' rule from פקדון, when he may have used a קל וחומר.

steps.title: The laughter was really about intentional versus unintentional
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the scholars laughed at the second difference in the ברייתא, that in פקדון an intentional oath is not treated like an unintentional one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the laughter was about 'an intentional one like an unintentional one,' as the ברייתא teaches: 'What about a פקדון? It is different, because there the Torah did not treat one who had an oath put on him like one who swore himself, and it did not treat an intentional oath like an unintentional one.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new explanation: the scholars laughed at the 'מזיד כשוגג' part of the ברייתא. It quotes the ברייתא's line again to show which words it means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the first difference (מושבע כנשבע) holds up, the scholars must have been mocking the second one (מזיד כשוגג). The גמרא repeats the same ברייתא line, but this time it points to its last words. The next step explains why this second difference seemed laughable.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the earlier idea and gives a new one)
Treating an intentional act the same as an unintentional one

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא line is quoted twice in this section, word for word. The first time, the laughter was thought to be about 'מושבע כנשבע'. The second time, it is about 'מזיד כשוגג'.

phrases.english: Rather, the laughter was about 'intentional like unintentional,'
as it teaches:
What about a deposit?
It is different, since [the Torah] did not make there
one who had an oath put on him like one who swore himself,
[or] an intentional one like an unintentional one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 12 rejected the first explanation, this gives a new one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moves the target of the laughter to the other half of the ברייתא's distinction.

steps.title: The scholars explain their joke: the word 'hidden' is missing in both cases
steps.stepSummary: The scholars argue that the reason an intentional oath counts for עדות also applies to פקדון, since ״וְנֶעֱלַם״ is missing in both.
steps.simpleTranslation: Think about it: how does he know that an intentional oath makes one liable for עדות? Because the word 'and it is hidden' is not written there. But here, by פקדון, that word is also not written!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out why the scholars found the second difference in the ברייתא funny. They say the reason given for עדות works just as well for פקדון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For עדות, an intentional false oath brings a קרבן because the תורה does not say ״וְנֶעֱלַם״ (that he forgot or did not realize). The פסוק about פקדון also does not say ״וְנֶעֱלַם״. So, the scholars argue, an intentional oath should count by פקדון too, and the ברייתא's difference makes no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: Think about it; now, since (opens a logical argument)
On purpose; knowing it was false
"And it is hidden": the sin happened without his realizing
From where does he know it?

phrases.english: Now, an intentional oath regarding testimony,
from where does he know it?
Because "and it is hidden" is not written there;
phrases.notes: He means: the תורה never says the person didn't realize, so it doesn't matter if he did it on purpose.

phrases.english: here too, "and it is hidden" is not written!
phrases.notes: "Here" means the oath about a deposit.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּדֵי מֵזִיד גַּבֵּי עֵדוּת מְנָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the laughter identified in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that in פקדון an intentional oath is not like an unintentional one
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same missing word (״וְנֶעֱלַם״) that makes intentional oaths count for עדות is also missing for פקדון, so the two should be treated the same.

steps.title: רב הונא: maybe רבי שמעון learned it from מעילה
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא defends רבי שמעון: the rule that an intentional oath does not count for פקדון may come from מעילה, where only an unintentional act brings a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said to them: What is so funny? Maybe רבי שמעון learned that by פקדון an intentional oath is not like an unintentional one from מעילה!
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא pushes back against the scholars. He says רבי שמעון did not need the word ״וְנֶעֱלַם״ for פקדון, because he had a different source: מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By מעילה (using הקדש property), a קרבן is brought only for an unintentional act. If רבי שמעון compared פקדון to מעילה, then an intentional oath by פקדון would not bring a קרבן either. So the missing ״וְנֶעֱלַם״ does not settle the question.

keyTerms.meaning: A joke; something to laugh at
Using הקדש (holy property) for personal benefit
Unintentional; by mistake
He learned it (from another case)

phrases.english: Rav Huna said to them:
And what is the joke?
Perhaps the rule that an intentional oath is not like an unintentional one in a deposit
Rabbi Shimon learned from misuse of holy property!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב הוּנָא: וּמַאי חוּכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the scholars' argument from step 14 by giving רבי שמעון a different source.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The scholars' assumption that the missing ״וְנֶעֱלַם״ must decide the rule for פקדון
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: They ignored that רבי שמעון could learn the פקדון rule from מעילה, which applies only when the act is unintentional.

steps.title: The scholars: that is exactly the joke
steps.stepSummary: The scholars answer that learning from מעילה is the very thing that is funny, since פקדון should be learned from עדות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And that is the joke: instead of learning it from מעילה, let him learn it from עדות!
steps.whatsHappening: The scholars defend their laughter. They agree רבי שמעון may have used מעילה, and they say that choice is exactly what they find strange.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is now which case פקדון should be compared to. The scholars think עדות is the natural match, since both are oaths in the same section. Learning from עדות would make an intentional oath count by פקדון too.

keyTerms.meaning: And that is the joke
Instead of
Let him learn

phrases.english: And that is the joke:
instead of learning it from misuse of holy property,
let him learn it from testimony!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב הונא's challenge by turning his explanation into the target of the laughter.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepts the other side's point and moves the problem to the choice of source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב הונא thought pointing to מעילה would remove the reason to laugh.
steps.terutzMaskana: The laughter stands: comparing פקדון to עדות seems more natural than comparing it to מעילה.

steps.title: Learning from מעילה makes more sense because of the shared word
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the scholars' point: רבי שמעון correctly learned from מעילה, because the פסוק about פקדון uses the word ״מְעִילָה״ just like the פסוק about הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that he should learn from מעילה, since it is learning 'מְעִילָה' from 'מְעִילָה'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sides with רבי שמעון and רב הונא. Comparing פקדון to מעילה is the better choice, so there was nothing to laugh at.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about פקדון says ״וּמָעֲלָה מַעַל״, the same word the תורה uses for מעילה in הקדש. The גמרא argues that this shared word makes מעילה the natural source. If so, the rule of מעילה (only an unintentional act brings a קרבן) carries over to פקדון. The next step challenges this.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense; it stands to reason
To learn (one case from another)
Since; because

phrases.english: It stands to reason that from misuse of holy property
he should learn it,
since it is "misuse" learned from "misuse."
phrases.notes: Both פסוקים use the word for misuse: ויקרא 5:21 (deposit) and ויקרא 5:15 (holy property).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the scholars' answer in step 16 and confirms רב הונא's view.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The scholars' claim that פקדון should be learned from עדות
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: They overlooked that פקדון and מעילה share the same word in the פסוקים, which makes מעילה the stronger source.

steps.title: Learn from testimony, because both say "shall sin"
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: פקדון should be learned from עדות, since both פסוקים use the word ״תֶּחֱטָא״.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary, he should have learned it from שבועת העדות, because both say ״תֶּחֱטָא״.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea from step 17. It argues that פקדון should be compared to עדות, not to מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 linked פקדון to מעילה through the shared word ״מְעִילָה״. This step points out a matching word between פקדון and עדות as well: ״תֶּחֱטָא״. If a shared word is enough, עדות is just as good a source, and there an intentional oath does count.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary; the opposite is true
He should have learned (derived) it
"Shall sin", a word found in both the עדות and פקדון פסוקים

phrases.english: On the contrary, he should have learned it from testimony,
since it is "shall sin" learned from "shall sin"!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:1 (עדות) and ויקרא 5:21 (פקדון) both use this word.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 17's choice of מעילה as the source for פקדון
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's derivation of פקדון from מעילה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A shared word also links פקדון to עדות (״תֶּחֱטָא״), so עדות is an equally valid source, and there an intentional oath counts.

steps.title: Misuse shares more features with deposit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that it makes more sense to learn from מעילה, because פקדון and מעילה share six features.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that he should learn from מעילה, because they share: the word מעילה, applying to everyone, benefiting from what is not yours, a fixed offering, adding a חומש, and an אשם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the challenge of step 18. It lists many points that פקדון and מעילה have in common.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When two sources are possible, you learn from the one that looks more like the case. The גמרא gives a memory list of six shared features: the word ״מְעִילָה״, it applies to all people, a person benefits from something not his, the קרבן is fixed, he adds a חומש, and he brings an אשם. Because of all these, מעילה is the better source.

keyTerms.meaning: It stands to reason; it makes more sense
Gets benefit from something
Fixed, a קרבן with one set value, not one that changes with a person's wealth
An extra fifth added when paying back
A guilt-offering

phrases.english: It stands to reason that he should have learned it from misuse,
since: misuse; with everyone; he benefits;
phrases.notes: These are short memory words. Each one names a feature that פקדון and מעילה share.

phrases.english: with a fixed offering; a fifth; and a guilt-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 18 by showing that מעילה is more similar to פקדון
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that עדות is the preferred source for פקדון
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: One shared word is not enough when another source shares many more features

steps.title: Testimony also shares many features with deposit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back again, listing features that פקדון shares with עדות.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary, he should have learned it from עדות, because they share: the word חטא, ordinary people's property, an oath, a claim and a denial, and the repeated word ״אוֹ״.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 19 with its own list. It shows that עדות also has many points in common with פקדון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This list matches the method of step 19: the word ״חֵטְא״, both involve ordinary property and not הקדש, both are done with an oath, both involve a claim that the person denies, and both פסוקים repeat the word "or". So עדות seems to be a strong source too.

keyTerms.meaning: Sin, the shared word ״תֶּחֱטָא״
An ordinary person, his property, as opposed to הקדש
He claimed from him and he denied it
The repeated word ״אוֹ״ ("or") in the פסוקים

phrases.english: On the contrary, he should have learned it from testimony,
since: sin; an ordinary person; with an oath;
he claimed from him and he denied him; and the "or"s!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדְּרַבָּה – מֵעֵדוּת הֲוָה לֵיהּ לְמֵילַף, שֶׁכֵּן חֵטְא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Counters step 19's list with a list of shared features between פקדון and עדות
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 19 that מעילה is clearly the more similar source
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: עדות also shares many features with פקדון, so the case for מעילה is not clearly stronger.

steps.title: The misuse list is longer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the features shared with מעילה are more numerous, so מעילה wins.
steps.simpleTranslation: These, the features shared with מעילה, are more numerous.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the debate. מעילה has more in common with פקדון than עדות does, so רבי שמעון was right to learn from מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When two sources each share features with a case, you follow the one with more shared features. The מעילה list is longer than the עדות list. This confirms that an intentional oath does not count for פקדון, just as only an unintentional act brings a קרבן for מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: These
More numerous; there are more of them

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון learns פקדון from מעילה, not from עדות, because מעילה shares more features with it. So in פקדון only an unintentional oath brings a קרבן.

phrases.english: These are more numerous.
phrases.notes: "These" means the list shared with מעילה, which is longer than the עדות list.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 20 by comparing the length of the two lists
steps.terutzResolutionType: Weighing which source has more shared features
steps.terutzHavaAmina: עדות might be an equal or better source for פקדון
steps.terutzMaskana: מעילה shares more features, so it is the correct source, and רבי שמעון's ruling holds

steps.title: So what was the joke?
steps.stepSummary: Since every difficulty with רבי שמעון has been answered, the גמרא asks what the scholars were laughing at.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what was the joke?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reopens the question from step 9. It has defended the ברייתא, so it now asks what the scholars found funny. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 14 through 21 showed that רבי שמעון's rule for פקדון makes sense. So the laughing cannot have been about that rule. The גמרא now has to find another reason the scholars laughed.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, what...? (a question asked after an earlier idea falls away)
A joke; something to laugh at

phrases.english: Rather, what is the joke?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the defense of רבי שמעון succeeds, returns to the original question of why the scholars laughed
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the scholars actually found funny in the ברייתא, since the פקדון rule has been defended

steps.title: רב פפא and רב הונא explain the joke
steps.stepSummary: The 'joke' was that רבי שמעון learns a גזירה שוה between פקדון and עדות, yet still points out differences between them.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב פפא and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע came back from their teacher's study hall, they said: This is what the scholars laughed at. רבי שמעון learns the law through a גזירה שוה. So why does he also object, 'A פקדון is different, because there the תורה did not treat someone made to swear like someone who swore himself, and did not treat a deliberate oath like an accidental one'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 22, 'what were the scholars laughing at?' רב פפא and רב הונא say they were laughing at what looks like a contradiction in רבי שמעון's method.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזירה שוה makes the two oaths fully alike, so pointing out differences between them should no longer matter. Yet רבי שמעון does point out two differences: מושבע versus נשבע, and מזיד versus שוגג. To the scholars, using both arguments at once looked self-defeating.

keyTerms.meaning: A joke, something worth laughing at
Learning one law from another because the Torah uses the same word in both places
He objects, he points out a difference
Someone made to swear by others, treated like someone who swore on his own
A deliberate act treated like an accidental one

phrases.english: When Rav Pappa came

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ מִבֵּי רַב,
phrases.english: and Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua, from the study hall,
they said: This is the joke:

phrases.aramaic: מִכְּדֵי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה גְּמִיר,
phrases.english: after all, Rabbi Shimon learns it through a verbal analogy,
phrases.notes: This is the ״תֶּחֱטָא״ link between פקדון and עדות from Step 18.

phrases.english: so why does he need to object:
What about a deposit? It is special in that
the Torah did not treat one made to swear like one who swore,
phrases.notes: 'Made to swear' means someone else put the oath on him, and he just answered 'אמן.'

phrases.english: or a deliberate one like an accidental one?

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב פָּפָּא וְרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ מִבֵּי רַב, אָמְרִי: הַיְינוּ חוּכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 22 by naming what the scholars found laughable.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The scholars laughed because רבי שמעון relies on a גזירה שוה, yet still points out differences that the גזירה שוה should erase.

steps.title: It is not a joke: the objection came before the גזירה שוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the laughter: רבי שמעון may have objected only before he had the גזירה שוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is so funny? Maybe רבי שמעון raised his objection before the גזירה שוה was established for him. Once he had the גזירה שוה, he no longer objects.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי שמעון. It says his two arguments belong to two different stages, so they do not contradict each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first, רבי שמעון compared the oaths by logic, and at that stage he could point out differences. Once he received the גזירה שוה, the differences no longer counted. That would mean a false deposit oath brings a קרבן even when someone else put the oath on him, and even when he lied on purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: Before
After
That it became established for him (that he had it as a tradition)

phrases.english: And what is the joke?
Perhaps when he objected,
it was before the verbal analogy was established for him;
after the verbal analogy was established for him,
he does not object!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the joke described in Step 23.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that רבי שמעון's objection and his גזירה שוה contradict each other.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The laughter assumes both arguments were held at the same time. They may belong to two different stages.

steps.title: But רבא בר איתי says רבי שמעון gives no atonement for a deliberate deposit oath
steps.stepSummary: A teaching of רבא בר איתי shows that רבי שמעון still separates deliberate from accidental for a deposit oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: He doesn't object anymore? But רבא בר איתי said to the scholars: Who taught that a deliberate false deposit oath cannot be atoned for with a קרבן? It is רבי שמעון!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 24. It brings proof that even in his final view, רבי שמעון kept one of the differences.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי שמעון had fully dropped his objections after the גזירה שוה, a deliberate false deposit oath would bring a קרבן, just like an accidental one. But רבא בר איתי says רבי שמעון holds that the deliberate version gets no קרבן atonement. So at least the מזיד/שוגג difference still stands for him.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who identified the source of this teaching
Its deliberate version
Was not given atonement (a קרבן does not atone for it)

phrases.english: And he does not object?!

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר לְהוּ רָבָא בַּר אִיתַּי לְרַבָּנַן:
phrases.english: But Rava bar Ittai said to the Sages:
Who is the one who taught that for an oath on a deposit
the deliberate version is not given atonement?
It is Rabbi Shimon!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא?! וְהָאָמַר לְהוּ רָבָא בַּר אִיתַּי לְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges Step 24's claim that רבי שמעון dropped his objections after the גזירה שוה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that after the גזירה שוה, רבי שמעון no longer separates פקדון from עדות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא בר איתי says רבי שמעון still separates deliberate from accidental for a deposit oath. So the objections did not fully disappear.

steps.title: He keeps the deliberate/accidental difference but drops the other one
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון still separates deliberate from accidental, learning that from מעילה, but he no longer separates someone made to swear from someone who swore.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps רבי שמעון still objects on the point of deliberate versus accidental. That is because on this point he learns the deposit oath from מעילה, since the features they share are more numerous. But he no longer objects on the point of someone made to swear versus someone who swore himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by splitting רבי שמעון's two objections. One survives the גזירה שוה and the other does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the question of a deliberate oath, רבי שמעון learns פקדון from מעילה. As Steps 19 and 21 showed, פקדון shares more features with מעילה than with עדות, and מעילה gives no קרבן for a deliberate act. On the question of מושבע versus נשבע, the גזירה שוה with עדות wins, so the deposit oath is the same as the testimony oath there.

keyTerms.meaning: Misusing הקדש property, which brings a קרבן only when done by accident
More numerous
He learns it (derives the law)

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי שמעון, the deposit oath follows עדות through the גזירה שוה on מושבע כנשבע, so a man made to swear by others is also liable. But it follows מעילה on מזיד, so a deliberate false oath gets no קרבן, because פקדון has more in common with מעילה.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי שמעון either keeps both objections or drops both. He keeps one (מזיד/שוגג) and drops the other (מושבע/נשבע).

phrases.english: Perhaps on deliberate like accidental he does object,
since he learns it from misuse of consecrated property,
since those are more numerous;
phrases.notes: 'Those' means the shared features between פקדון and מעילה from Step 19.

phrases.english: but on one made to swear like one who swore, he does not object.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of Step 25 by splitting רבי שמעון's two objections.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the case: one objection still stands and the other is cancelled by the גזירה שוה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe the גזירה שוה cancels all of רבי שמעון's objections, which would clash with רבא בר איתי.
steps.terutzMaskana: The מזיד/שוגג objection stays, learned from מעילה. The מושבע/נשבע objection is cancelled by the גזירה שוה.

steps.title: Testimony should learn the deliberate–accidental split from deposit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי שמעון: if פקדון learns from מעילה that a deliberate false oath brings no קרבן, then עדות should learn the same thing from פקדון through the גזירה שוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let עדות go back and learn from פקדון that deliberate is not like accidental. Just as with פקדון, accidental — yes, deliberate — no, so too with עדות, accidental — yes, deliberate — no. This works the same way that he learns פקדון from מעילה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer in Step 26. If רבי שמעון learns from מעילה that only an accidental deposit oath brings a קרבן, the גזירה שוה should pass that same rule on to the oath of testimony.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a chain of learning here. First, מעילה teaches פקדון that a deliberate false oath does not bring a קרבן. Then the גזירה שוה between פקדון and עדות should pass that rule on to עדות. The problem is that שבועת העדות brings a קרבן even for a deliberate false oath, so the chain seems to give the wrong result.

keyTerms.meaning: And let it go back. Here it means: let the oath of testimony turn back and learn from the deposit oath.
And let it learn, meaning let it take a rule from another case
On purpose. Here it means someone who knowingly swore falsely.
By accident. Here it means someone who swore falsely without realizing the oath or its weight.
Short for שְׁבוּעַת הָעֵדוּת, a false oath denying that one knows testimony
Yes / no, meaning he is liable / he is not liable

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two directions of learning. מעילה teaches פקדון. The challenge now is that פקדון should in turn teach עדות through the גזירה שוה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This challenge tests how far the גזירה שוה reaches. Does it carry over every rule that פקדון has, even a rule that פקדון itself learned from somewhere else?

phrases.english: Then let the oath of testimony go back
phrases.notes: He means: let עדות go back to the גזירה שוה it shares with פקדון.

phrases.english: and learn it from the deposit oath,
that deliberate is not like accidental:

phrases.aramaic: מָה פִּקָּדוֹן, שׁוֹגֵג אִין מֵזִיד לָא;
phrases.english: just as with a deposit, accidental — yes, deliberate — no;
phrases.notes: Yes means he brings a קרבן; no means he does not.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עֵדוּת, שׁוֹגֵג אִין מֵזִיד לָא –
phrases.english: so too with testimony, accidental — yes, deliberate — no,
just as he learns deposit from misuse of holy property!
phrases.notes: This points back to Step 26, where רבי שמעון learned the split for deposit from מעילה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in Step 26 by passing its rule on to עדות through the גזירה שוה.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 26's claim that רבי שמעון learns the deliberate–accidental split for פקדון from מעילה, while still using the גזירה שוה between פקדון and עדות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If פקדון has the split, the גזירה שוה should give עדות the same split. But שבועת העדות makes a person liable even for a deliberate false oath.
